CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate ongoing management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for a follow-up visit, expressing mixed feelings regarding his treatment regimen. He reports that his sleep quality has shown slight improvement, with an average of 7.5 hours per night, although he still struggles with sleep onset. He acknowledges that the trazodone at 75 mg continues to help reduce nocturnal awakenings, yet he experiences intermittent episodes of restlessness, particularly on nights before work deadlines.
Mr. Smith reports that his fatigue has persisted, particularly during peak work periods, stating that he feels mentally and physically drained. He notes that his headaches have remained consistent in frequency, occurring approximately three times per week, with an average intensity of 6 out of 10. He has been utilizing ibuprofen more frequently, about 3-4 times weekly, to manage these headaches, which he describes as increasingly debilitating.
Despite these challenges, Mr. Smith has maintained his commitment to his holistic treatment plan, regularly attending acupuncture sessions and participating in yoga classes. He has also increased his mindfulness practice, which he feels has been beneficial for his overall anxiety management. However, he expresses a desire for more effective coping mechanisms to manage the stress associated with his job.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (increased usage noted) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that the pressure from project deadlines remains a significant stressor. He actively participates in yoga and meditation, which he finds helpful. He abstains from alcohol and follows a primarily plant-based diet, although he admits to occasionally indulging in processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist; anxiety remains manageable but has increased slightly due to work stress; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has stabilized; intensity is slightly higher; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, and appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Recommend additional therapy sessions focused on cognitive-behavioral strategies for work-related stress management. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg; explore sleep hygiene strategies and consider a sleep study if sleep onset issues persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly. Given the increased frequency and intensity of headaches, initiate topiramate at 25 mg daily for preventive therapy, titrating as needed based on response. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued physical activity and mindfulness practices. Refer to a nutritionist for dietary optimization, particularly during high-stress periods.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-07-01 to assess ongoing symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
